note: Do not edit by hand. Re-run the script after changing any diagnostic in packages/*/src.

2.topic: Parse, overlay, alias resolution, tier validation

codes.message: No ds.config.ts found in ${root}
codes.help: Run `girih init` to scaffold a workspace, or cd into an existing one.

codes.message: Failed to load ${configPath}: ${message.split('\n')[0]}
codes.help: The error comes from ds.config.ts itself. It is evaluated as real TypeScript, so a syntax error, an unresolved import, or a throw at module scope all land here.

codes.message: Config is missing 'name' (the published package name, e.g. '@acme/design-system').
codes.help: Add `name: '@scope/design-system'`. It is the name the generated package is published under, so it has to be one you own.

codes.message: Brand '${brand.name}' points at a missing token file: ${brand.tokensFile}
codes.help: Create the overlay file (an empty {} is valid) or fix brands.definitions.${brand.name}.tokens.

codes.message: Config must define at least one brand under brands.definitions.
codes.help: Add one: `brands: { default: 'base', definitions: { base: { tokens: 'brands/base/tokens.json' } } }`. An empty {} overlay is valid, so the default brand can override nothing.

codes.message: brands.default ('${raw.brands?.default}') is not a key of brands.definitions.
codes.help: Known brands: ${Object.keys(definitions).join(', ')}

codes.message: ds.config.ts must default-export a config object (use defineConfig).
codes.help: Write `export default defineConfig({ … })`. A named export is not read, and neither is a default that is not an object.

codes.message: Unknown brand '${options.brand}'.
codes.help: Known brands: ${[...build.graphs.keys()].join(', ')}.

codes.message: Generated file ${path} was edited by hand since the last \`girih generate\`.
codes.help: Undo the edit or eject the component (M5); the next generate will refuse to overwrite it.

codes.message: .ds/manifest.json is corrupt or from an incompatible girih version — drift detection is disabled.
codes.help: Delete .ds/manifest.json and regenerate.

codes.message: '${name}' is recorded as ejected in ds.lock, but ${path} is missing.
codes.help: Restore the file, or remove the '${name}' entry from ds.lock to return to generation.

codes.message: ds.lock is corrupt or from an incompatible girih version.
codes.help: ds.lock is machine-managed and committed — restore it from git history.

codes.message: '${name}' was ejected from a different spec/template than the current one — the fork may not honor the contract anymore.
codes.help: Review the fork against the current spec, or re-eject after removing the ds.lock entry (`girih forks` reports this; the 3-way merge is not built yet).

codes.message: ds.lock records '${name}' as ejected, but no spec with that name exists — the fork is not generated.
codes.help: Restore design/components/${kebabName(name)}/${kebabName(name)}.contract.ts, or remove the ds.lock entry.

codes.message: Failed to write '${file.path}': ${(error as Error).message}
codes.help: Check that the output directory is writable and that there is free disk space.

codes.message: Token file must be a JSON object at the top level.
codes.help: A DTCG token file is an object of groups and tokens. An array or a bare value at the top level cannot be merged with the others.

codes.message: Token or group name '${key}' contains a character forbidden by DTCG ('.', '{', '}').
codes.help: Those three characters delimit token paths and references, so a name containing one could never be referenced. Rename the token or group.

codes.message: '${[...segments, key].join('.')}' is a bare ${typeof child}; tokens must be objects with a $value.
codes.help: Write it as { "$value": ${JSON.stringify(child)} }.

codes.message: Cannot infer the tier of '${file}' from its name — assuming 'semantic'.
codes.help: Name token files global*.tokens.json / semantic*.tokens.json, or put component tokens under a components/ directory — design/components/<name>/<name>.tokens.json in the default layout.

codes.message: Cannot read token file: ${(error as Error).message}
codes.help: Check the path and that the file is readable. A token file glob that matches a directory or a broken symlink lands here too.

codes.message: No token files matched ${config.tokens.source.join(', ')} under ${config.root}.
codes.help: legacyTokenLayoutHint(config) ?? 'Create design/tokens/global.tokens.json to get started.'

codes.message: Token or group name '${key}' contains characters that do not translate cleanly to CSS variable names.
codes.help: Stick to lowercase letters, digits, "-" and "_" so generated names stay predictable.

codes.message: Unknown '$'-prefixed property '${key}' is ignored (the '$' prefix is reserved by DTCG).
codes.help: Known properties: ${[...KNOWN_DOLLAR_PROPS].join(', ')}. Rename the key if it was meant to be a group.

codes.message: '${path}' is a token (it has a $value) but also contains '${key}' — tokens cannot nest groups or other tokens.
codes.help: Move '${key}' out to a sibling group, e.g. '${path}-${key}'.

codes.message: Token '${token.path}' is defined in both ${existing.file} and ${token.file}.
codes.help: Every token path must have exactly one definition; brand overlays are the only sanctioned override.

codes.message: Token '${token.path}' is nested under '${shadowedAncestor}', which is itself a token (defined in ${tokens.get(shadowedAncestor)!.file}).
codes.help: A path must be either a token or a group, never both — rename one of them.

codes.message: Cannot parse token file as JSON: ${(error as Error).message}
codes.help: Check for a trailing comma, an unquoted key, or other invalid JSON — DTCG token files are plain JSON, no comments allowed.

codes.message: Brand overlay introduces '${token.path}', which does not exist in the base token set.
codes.help: Overlays may only override existing tokens. Define the token in tokens/ first, then override its value here.

codes.message: Brand overlay changes the $type of '${token.path}' from '${baseToken.type}' to '${token.type}'.
codes.help: A brand may change a token value, never its type — types are part of the shared contract.

codes.message: '${token.path}' references '{${ref}}', which does not exist.
codes.help: Check the spelling and the tier. A reference is the full dotted path from the top of the token set, not a path relative to the current group.

codes.message: Circular token reference: ${cycle.map((p) => `'${p}'`).join(' → ')}.
codes.help: Break the cycle by pointing one of these tokens at a raw value.

codes.message: Failed to resolve '${token.path}': ${(error as Error).message}
codes.help: Usually a malformed $value. Aliases must be a single reference in braces; anything else is treated as a literal.

codes.message: ${token.tier} token '${token.path}' references ${target.tier} token '{${ref}}' — references must flow component → semantic → global, never upward.
codes.help: Tier references only ever flow downward: component to semantic to global. Move the value down a tier, or point at something lower.

codes.message: component token '${token.path}' references global token '{${ref}}' directly, skipping the semantic tier.
codes.help: Introduce a semantic alias for '{${ref}}' so brands can re-theme it without touching component tokens.

codes.message: '${token.path}' ($type '${token.type}') aliases '{${ref}}' which has $type '${target.type}'.
codes.help: Give both tokens the same $type, or drop $type from the alias so it inherits from its target.

codes.message: Brand '${brand}' does not resolve the same token set as '${brands[0]}':
codes.help: A brand overlay may override an existing path but never add or remove one, so every brand has to be structurally identical. Move an extra token into the base set, or add the missing one there.

codes.message: CSS generation failed for brand '${brand}': ${(error as Error).message}
codes.help: Usually a token value style-dictionary cannot serialise. GIRIH3002 names the specific variable when it can identify one.

codes.message: '${variable}' (brand '${brand}') has a composite value no CSS transform could flatten.
codes.help: Give the token a supported $type (shadow, typography, border, transition, cubicBezier, fontFamily) or split it into scalar tokens.

codes.message: Tokens ${paths.map((p) => `'${p}'`).join(' and ')} both map to the CSS variable '${varName}'.
codes.help: Rename one of them — CSS variable names are case-insensitive here and join segments with "-".

codes.message: Component name '${ir.name}' must be PascalCase (it becomes an exported React identifier).
codes.help: The name becomes the exported React identifier, so it has to start with a capital: `name: 'Button'`. The spec file itself stays kebab-case.
Every brand must resolve the same token set, so the token has to exist in the base tokens — a brand overlay may override paths but never introduce them.

codes.message: ${ctx.subject} references global token '{${path}}' at ${ctx.where} — consume semantic or component tokens instead.
codes.help: Add a semantic token that aliases this global one and reference that instead. A value bound straight to a global cannot be re-themed per brand.

codes.message: Component '${ir.name}' is defined more than once (${seen.get(ir.name)} and ${file}).
codes.help: Two spec files declare the same name, and the name decides the emitted component — so one would overwrite the other. Rename one or delete the duplicate.

codes.message: Variant axis '${axis.axis}' of '${ir.name}' has no values.
codes.help: Give the axis at least one value, or remove it — an axis with no values emits a prop that can never be set.

codes.message: Variant axis '${axis.axis}' of '${ir.name}' defaults to '${axis.default}', which is not one of [${axis.values.join(', ')}].
codes.help: Set default to one of the listed values, or add the missing value to values.

codes.message: '${ir.name}' declares state '${state}', which the '${ir.template}' template does not implement.
codes.help: States of '${ir.template}': ${implementableStates.join(', ') || '(none)'}. States are template capability flags, not arbitrary behavior.

codes.message: '${ir.name}' styles variant axis '${block.axis}', which is not declared under variants.
codes.help: Declare the axis under variants first, or remove the style block — this CSS would never match anything.

codes.message: '${ir.name}' styles '${block.axis}.${block.value}', but '${block.value}' is not a declared value of that axis.
codes.help: Add it to that axis's values, or correct the spelling.

codes.message: '${ir.name}' styles state '${state.state}' under tokens.states, but does not declare that state.
codes.help: Declare it under states first. Declaring a state is what makes the template wire it up, so styling alone would emit CSS that nothing ever matches.

codes.message: ${ctx.subject} has a malformed token reference '${ref}' at ${ctx.where} — expected '{token.path}'.
codes.help: A reference is one token path in braces: `{color.action}`. No nesting, no fallback value, no spaces.

codes.message: '${ir.name}' ${what} '${name}' is not a valid camelCase identifier — it becomes a React prop.
codes.help: It is destructured by name in the generated component, so it must be a plain camelCase identifier — no dashes, no spaces, not starting with a digit.

codes.message: '${spec.name}' has a non-string declaration for '${property}' at ${where} — every styled value must be a '{token.path}' reference.
codes.help: Did you mean to nest '${property}' under a 'states' key?

codes.message: '${ir.name}' styles unknown CSS property '${property}' at ${where} — it will be emitted verbatim.
codes.help: Check the spelling. If it really is a custom or very new property, this warning is expected — the declaration is emitted exactly as written.

codes.message: '${ir.name}' maps aria attributes to state '${aria.state}', which it does not declare under states.
codes.help: Add the state to states, or drop the aria mapping. girih only wires aria for states the component declares.

codes.message: '${ir.name}' renders '<${ir.element}>', which is not a known host element.
codes.help: Known elements: ${[...KNOWN_ELEMENTS].join(', ')}.

codes.message: Failed to load spec: ${(error as Error).message}
codes.help: The spec is evaluated as real TypeScript, so a syntax error, an unresolved import, or a throw at module scope all land here.

codes.message: ${file} does not default-export a component spec.
codes.help: Export the result of defineSpec({...}) from '@faravahar/girih'.

codes.message: ${file} contains a non-serializable value at '${impure}' — specs must be pure data.
codes.help: Remove functions, dates, class instances, and symbols; a spec is a contract, not a program.

codes.message: No contracts matched '${config.components.specs}', but ${found.length} '${legacyGlob}' file${plural} ${found.length === 1 ? 'is' : 'are'} present (${found.slice(0, 3).join(', ')}${found.length > 3 ? ', …' : ''}).
codes.help: advice

codes.message: ${file} does not default-export a variant extension.
codes.help: Export the result of defineVariant({ name, extends, tokens }) from '@faravahar/girih'.

codes.message: Failed to load extension: ${(error as Error).message}
codes.help: The extension is evaluated as real TypeScript, so a syntax error, an unresolved import, or a throw at module scope all land here.

codes.message: Extension name '${extension.name}' must be PascalCase (it becomes an exported React identifier).
codes.help: The name becomes the exported React identifier, so it has to start with a capital. The .ext.ts file itself stays kebab-case.

codes.message: Extension '${extension.name}' collides with an existing component or extension.
codes.help: Every component and extension shares one export namespace, because they all become named exports of the same package. Rename this one.

codes.message: Extension '${extension.name}' extends '${extension.extends}', which is not in the component catalog.
codes.help: Known components: ${[...byName.keys()].join(', ') || '(none)'}.

codes.message: '${extension.extends}' does not allow extensions (extensibility.allowExtends is false).
codes.help: Set extensibility.allowExtends: true on the base contract, if extending it is genuinely intended.

codes.message: Extension '${extension.name}' overrides '${property}', which '${extension.extends}' does not list under extensibility.overridableTokens.
codes.help: Overridable: ${base.extensibility.overridableTokens.join(', ') || '(none)'}.

codes.message: '${extension.extends}' is a compound (dialog) component — extensions can only build on single-element components.
codes.help: A compound component emits several parts, so there is no single element for a wrapper to forward props to. Extend one of the single-element components instead.

codes.message: ${ctx.subject} reaches into '{${path}}', another component's token namespace, at ${ctx.where}.
codes.help: Use semantic tokens or '${ctx.ownNamespace}.*' tokens so this survives refactors of unrelated components.

codes.message: '${ir.name}' uses template '${ir.template}', which this girih version does not ship.
codes.help: Available templates: ${Object.keys(templates).join(', ')}.

codes.message: '${ir.name}' styles part '${part.part}', which the '${ir.template}' template does not have.
codes.help:
declaredParts.size > 0
            ? `Parts of '${ir.template}': ${[...declaredParts].join(', ')}.`
            : `The '${ir.template}' template has no parts — use tokens.base.`

codes.message: '${ir.name}' declares variant axis '${axis.axis}', but the '${ir.template}' template only wires up: ${template.variantAxes.join(', ')}.
codes.help: A silently-ignored axis would validate and then do nothing — declare only axes the template implements.

codes.message: '${ir.name}' maps aria attributes to state '${aria.state}', which the '${ir.template}' template only expresses in CSS — the attributes are not wired.
codes.help: Move the aria mapping to a component whose template wires attributes, or drop it — leaving it in place would imply accessibility support that is not emitted.

codes.message: No TypeScript sources in ${srcDir} — run \`girih generate react\` first.
codes.help: The build compiles generated source, so there is nothing to compile until `girih generate react` has written it.

codes.message: The generated package imports ${missing.map((m) => `'${m}'`).join(', ')}, which ${missing.length === 1 ? 'is' : 'are'} not installed.
codes.help: Install the build prerequisites: ${addDevCommand(detectPackageManager(), missing)}
